completion_evidence_required: List every changed path and identify the app query entry point and the single dashboard socket assign.
Show focused test evidence that the query refetches active clubs from authenticated email on every call and rejects a selected club after membership loss despite a stale mount-time snapshot.
Show focused LiveView evidence that route/access semantics and successful refresh behavior remain correct after projection-backed fields move under the coherent dashboard result.
Show evidence that at least one meaningful transient dashboard state survives a successful query-result replacement, with the remaining existing admission, removal and targeted-add suites passing.

Confirm by source inspection that connected subscription occurs before the query call, refreshes no longer authorize through `current_identity_clubs`, and existing notification predicates were not broadened or presented as the final adapter.
Report the exact focused validation commands, exit statuses and concise pass summaries, plus any unresolved issue without marking the task complete.
constraints: Preserve every existing dashboard URL, rendered DOM contract and user-visible behavior; this task introduces a read boundary, not a visual redesign.

The authenticated normalized email is the durable query input. A stale `current_identity_clubs` snapshot may remain only if another unchanged shell concern requires it, but it must not authorize the dashboard query or refresh.

The coherent dashboard result is the source of truth for projection-backed display and authorization fields. Do not retain compatibility mirrors for selected club/group, members, counts, messages or permissions in socket state.
A render-local expansion of the dashboard map is allowed to keep the template change bounded because it does not create independently refreshed socket state.
Subscribe only for a connected LiveView and do so before the connected query invocation. Do not claim this ordering alone closes the bind-time race; task 004 owns deterministic reconciliation.

Preserve the existing manual notification predicates exactly enough to avoid expanding task scope. Their known over-broad and missing cases are intentional pending work, not behavior to bless as the target design.
Preserve existing `:forbidden` and `:not_found` transitions and never retain the previous private dashboard result when the fresh query returns an access error.
Keep active section, route IDs, targeted-member focus/success, picker form/query/open state, removal operation state, access-request state, flash and navigation outside the dashboard result.
Do not nest a new query or view-model module inside another module.
Use focused, deterministic tests and do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
outcome: The club dashboard loads and refreshes one coherent dashboard view model from the authenticated email and freshly resolved active-club authority, stores that result under one socket assign, subscribes before the connected initial read, and preserves existing route, access, rendering, command and transient-state behavior while the current notification predicates remain provisional.

references.facts: The technical model requires one coherent dashboard query result, fresh authorization on every refresh, LiveView-owned subscription, subscribe-before-read ordering and preservation of transient state. The broader bind-time reconciliation, scoped invalidation and conversation proof remain later obligations.

ADR 0027 requires each view-specific query to return one coherent view model for one assign, with an authorized reread on relevant changes; club home must begin as one dashboard model rather than separately refreshed fields.

Committed projection notifications are broadcast on the shared PubSub topic as `{:read_model_changed, %{projector: ..., source_event: ..., metadata: ..., changes: ...}}`. This task retains the dashboard's current filters but moves subscription before the connected read.

The accepted matrix records that MemberDashboardLive currently spreads one composed result across ordinary assigns, reads before subscribing and refreshes with mount-captured active clubs. It identifies route IDs, picker/admission/removal/access-request state as LiveView-owned and requires fresh authority beginning from authenticated email.

`mount/3` currently calls `MemberDashboardPresentation.load/4` before subscribing and fans `dashboard_assigns` into the socket. `refresh_dashboard/3` reuses `current_identity_clubs`; handlers and command helpers read selected club, selected group, current member and permission flags from top-level assigns. Existing handle_info clauses broadly refresh for all MemberEmailDelivery changes and same-club configured projectors.

`load/4` already composes selected club/member authorization, discoverable and participating groups, permissions, members, counts, conversations, admission candidates and group email data into one result map. It accepts caller-supplied active clubs, so the new query must supply a fresh list on every invocation while preserving `:forbidden` and `:not_found` distinctions.

`Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1` normalizes the email and reads the current active club projections. It is the required fresh starting point instead of `current_identity_clubs` captured during mount.

The dashboard template currently consumes flat assigns for selected club/group, groups, permissions, member rows, counts and message rows. Rendering may expand the coherent dashboard model locally, but these values must no longer be duplicated as long-lived socket assigns.

Existing coverage includes routed rendering, group discovery, access loss, route-patch authorization rechecks, current-actor role loss, conversation-access changes, member rows/counts and initial role badges. Extend focused coverage for the new query boundary, fresh active-club authority and transient-state preservation without claiming later interest-mapping proof.

Existing feature-level LiveView tests exercise admission/removal command behavior, projector-driven open-view updates and reconnect-sensitive command state. They must continue passing after dashboard fields move under one result assign.
Targeted-add coverage protects routed target resolution, confirmation, success/focus state and authorization behavior that must remain LiveView-owned across dashboard result replacement.

LiveView state changes should use assigns consistently; focused LiveView tests should assert rendered outcomes with selectors, and transient forms must remain `to_form/2`-backed rather than being replaced by query refreshes.
Keep modules in separate files, use focused Mix test files, and avoid sleeps in process tests; deterministic synchronization should be used where process ordering must be proved.
Any HEEx edits must retain component form usage, unique DOM IDs and valid HEEx interpolation and conditional syntax.

scope: Add an app-owned `MembaWeb.MemberDashboardQuery` boundary, with focused tests, that accepts the routed club identity, authenticated normalized email and selected group identity; every invocation must call `Accounts.list_active_clubs_for_email/1`, construct only the identity input needed by `MemberDashboardPresentation`, and return its coherent result or the existing `:forbidden`/`:not_found` error.

Change `MemberDashboardLive.mount/3`, `handle_params/3`, explicit command refreshes and notification refreshes to use the new query. On connected mount, subscribe to `Memba.ReadModelChanges.topic/0` before invoking the query; disconnected mount must still perform the current read.

Keep the routed club ID and authenticated identity email as stable LiveView inputs. Do not derive a later query input from the previously loaded `selected_club`, and do not use mount-captured `current_identity_clubs` as authorization for a refresh.

Store the projection-backed dashboard result under one long-lived socket assign such as `:dashboard`. Adapt event handlers and helper functions to read selected club, selected group, current member, permission flags, rows and counts from that model instead of retaining mirrored top-level socket assigns.

Adapt rendering to consume the coherent model without duplicating all of its fields into socket state. A render-local map expansion for the existing template is acceptable; if Phoenix shell metadata requires a derived `:page_title`, keep the dashboard result as its sole source and do not perform an independent read.

Preserve current `:forbidden` versus `:not_found` behavior on mount, route patches and refreshes, and preserve existing command behavior for access requests, admissions, removals and welcome delivery.

Retain the current hand-written `handle_info/2` matching semantics provisionally, including their current broad and missing cases. This slice changes their refresh target to the new query but does not introduce interests, a source adapter, bind-window reconciliation or new projector coverage.

Add focused proof that repeated query calls use fresh active-club authority, that selected-club membership loss cannot be masked by a mount-time club snapshot, that route changes still re-evaluate selected-group access, and that successful refreshes do not reset picker/query, targeted-add, removal, access-request or command feedback state. Preserve existing dashboard, admission and targeted-add regression coverage.
scope_exclusions: Do not implement the provisional generic binding, opaque interest matching, notification translator, bind-time reconciliation, reconnect contract or subscriber cleanup; those belong to tasks 004 and 005.

todo_line: - [ ] 003 Introduce and focused-test an app-owned dashboard query/view-model boundary that begins from the authenticated email and fresh active-club authority; move all projection-backed dashboard data behind one coherent socket assign, subscribe before the connected initial read, preserve route/access error semantics and transient LiveView state, and retain the existing notification predicates provisionally.
